info.title: Model Brewery Controller
info.description:
A loopback-only API for the Brewery workbench. Start with getState to discover configured workers, their capabilities, registered inputs, and saved prompts. The controller queues only the workflows described here. To convert a model, use createConversion: one request runs inspect, plan, convert and verify. Use createJob with one conversion kind only for a single diagnostic stage. Neither route qualifies a release. Worker and SSH configuration is operator-owned; there is no API for running shell commands or reading arbitrary files or the private controller data directory. putSettings saves benchmark and evaluation settings for a worker that the operator enrolled; it accepts only approved ports, approved suites and loopback endpoints. applyAdminAction changes controller policy under the same access rules as Settings. Its editor setup action installs a separate editor on an existing SSH worker without changing SSH trust or the original worker. Artifact paths in job results are worker-side references, not download URLs.

Send a single Host header for the actual loopback listen address/port or localhost on that port. If sent, Origin must be the matching http origin and Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin or none. Non-browser POST clients must send Content-Type: application/json, including for the bodyless cancel action. Unrecognized API paths or methods return a JSON error with status 404 or 405. The router also handles HEAD for GET paths with no response body, except that HEAD on the event stream returns 405.

get.summary: Follow controller changes with Server-Sent Events
get.description: Open this stream with after set to a getState snapshot's event_cursor, or reconnect with Last-Event-ID set to the last change ID processed. An explicit Last-Event-ID takes precedence over after. The cursor is exclusive: first replay retained changes with ID greater than the cursor, then stream new changes. If neither parameter is supplied, start live at the current cursor. The controller retains up to 1024 changes. A stale or ahead cursor gets a resync event with no ID and then the stream closes; fetch getState again and reconnect with its cursor. Treat change events as invalidation notices and use the normal read endpoints for data. Comment heartbeats every 15 seconds carry no event ID or data.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Exclusive cursor as nonnegative decimal digits, within the signed 64-bit range.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Single exclusive cursor. Decimal digits only; must fit in a nonnegative signed 64-bit integer. Takes precedence over after.

get.description: Reads the SHA-256 checked token scores in the latest check bundle for B. A must be its immediate parent. Sentences are ranked by absolute log-probability gain. The default slice shows the first ranked sentence. Positive log-probability gain means lower loss. Shares use the signed corpus net gain, so they can be negative or exceed 100%. A zero net gain gives null shares.

post.summary: Check a scratch revision and save the results
post.description: For native HGN, the source worker checks the stored child and immediate parent. It audits the decoded writers and compares full-vocabulary CPU forward scores on fixed prompts. Send the child SHA-256 without behavior_direction or registered_marker. For SafeTensors, the controller verifies both files. With private GGUF files, the local worker measures behavior. Optionally score reviewed holdouts with behavior_direction or one registered evaluation partition with registered_marker. Both options require two private GGUF files and passing integrity checks. Without opt-in, if either GGUF is missing or integrity fails, the controller saves an integrity-only bundle. For a compiled program, the local CPU runtime checks pinned inputs and runs all valid cases. Poll the returned job ID. Do not send measured values or job references.

get.summary: Read the administration state
get.description: Infrastructure state uses the same access rules as Settings. It lists dispatch hosts, their job admission and resource policy, editor status, legacy catalog workers and runtimes, and the latest 50 policy audit entries. For an existing SSH transport, weight_editor.setup lists the setup status, last configured directory and available credential IDs and labels. Reading state does not contact workers.

post.summary: Apply one administration action
post.description: Changes controller policy using normal Settings access. set_host_policy controls pause and restricts jobs; set_host_resources replaces bounded resource overrides. setup_weight_editor installs and verifies a separate editor on an existing admitted SSH worker using a configured provision credential and existing SSH trust. It does not change the ordinary worker or planner. set_weight_editor enables or disables an available local or verified SSH editor without installing software or granting other job permissions. These actions use the host policy revision.

200.description: The action was applied. The body is the new administration state.

400.description: The body is malformed, too large, not JSON, has an unknown field or action, or gives an invalid editor model directory.

409.description: The worker state does not allow the action, the readiness or runtime check failed, the request exceeds the pool ceiling, or the helper is not available. Editor setup also conflicts if the revision is stale, the worker is not an admitted SSH worker, the selected credential is not configured for that worker, or verification fails.

get.summary: Read the tensor catalog for custom HGN profiles
get.description: Returns the catalog that is embedded in the controller. It lists every tensor of the one supported architecture, the encoding that each built-in profile (v2 and ht43) gives it, whether a custom profile can change it (editable), and the signed byte difference from v2 to ht43 (delta_bytes). The bytes are computed from the layout of the catalog. They are not a measurement of a real output. The catalog_sha256 binds a custom profile to this catalog. The tensors that are not editable keep their built-in encoding.

200.description: The embedded catalog, as stored.

get.summary: Read the GGUF preset and tensor type catalog
get.description: Returns the pinned catalog that is embedded in the controller. presets are the whole-model recipes of the pinned upstream quantizer, with aliases. tensor_types are the raw types that the encoder can write. Both mark which entries need an imatrix. The catalog lists no type that the encoder cannot write: it has no IQ1_XXS, and it has no F32 preset. A name in the catalog is not a promise that a given model can use it: the quantizer decides per tensor, and the job fails if the result differs from the plan.

200.description: The embedded catalog, as stored.

get.summary: Preview both container choices for a saved profile
get.description: Read-only. The saved profile's encoder stays fixed. Its own container uses the existing workflow, subject to normal source and worker admission. The other container cannot be submitted. The experimental extension names a possible lossless path, not a requirement. A compatible exact stock export could suffice in the future. This preview does not test artifacts or runtimes. It provides no evidence of payload preservation, tensor coverage, or release qualification.

200.description: HGN and GGUF export options, in that order.

get.summary: List the saved custom profile revisions
get.description: Rows of both formats are mixed, oldest first. A GGUF row always has format gguf. An older HGN row can have no format. Each revision is immutable. A change is a new revision.

200.description: All saved revisions, oldest first.

post.summary: Save a custom profile as an immutable revision
post.description: The body picks the format. Without format, or with format hgn, the rules below apply. With format gguf the body is a preset plus optional exact-tensor type overrides, and the controller checks them against the pinned GGUF catalog; see getGgufCatalog. A GGUF profile has no size estimate. A custom HGN profile starts from a base (v2 or ht43) and lists tensors that use the other built-in encoding. It chooses between these two encodings only. It cannot create a new encoding. The controller checks the catalog digest, the name, and that every override names an editable tensor with the alternate encoding. It then computes the predicted size from the catalog and saves the profile under revision, the SHA-256 of the canonical recipe. Saving does not start a job. The same content gives the same revision. Use the revision as profile_revision in createConversion. The predicted size is a layout estimate from the catalog. It does not show the quality or the runtime accuracy of the converted model.

200.description: An identical revision exists. It is returned unchanged.

400.description: The catalog digest differs, the name is invalid, there are no overrides or more than 4096, or an override is unknown, not editable, or equal to the base.

post.summary: Check admission for a specific conversion request without starting it
post.description: Checks the selected source, auxiliary inputs, host or pool, profile and options. Sends no work to a worker and does not write to the controller store. A positive result does not reserve a worker or qualify a release.

200.description: Admission decision and setup blockers, if any.

post.summary: Start the default one-submit conversion workflow
post.description:
Default way to convert a model. One request makes the controller run the child jobs inspect, plan, convert and verify in this order on one worker. The controller stores the workflow, so it continues if the client disconnects, and resumes after a controller restart by using the stored child job IDs. A child job that was running and cannot be checked is not retried. The workflow stops at the first failed or cancelled child job. Later stages are not queued. The call does not wait for the worker. Poll getConversion, or follow the child jobs with getJob and streamEvents. There is no conversion event kind and no conversion key in capabilities; the child jobs use the normal job events. A succeeded workflow means that all four child jobs succeeded. It is not a release qualification, and it does not show model quality. To run an ordinary stage alone for diagnosis, use createJob. A managed GGUF layer recipe is accepted only by createConversion.

Host: omit host to use the source model's host. Set host to auto to use an eligible worker of the configured quantization pool. Set a worker ID to pin that worker. The workflow reports host auto as requested_host. A managed GGUF layer recipe must run on the source worker and does not accept auto.

It never starts a later stage. The response can show state running until the child job stops. Poll getConversion until the state is terminal. A repeat request, or a request for a terminal workflow, returns the current workflow. A timeout or a lost link is not proof that a worker stopped.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional single, case-sensitive key scoped to this create operation. A new successful request returns 201 and binds the key to the typed body and generated ID. A matching retry returns 200 with only the original ID and no new side effects, even if that object was deleted or the input catalog changed. For createConversion, it returns the current conversion workflow. For intervention writes, it returns the original immutable version. A different typed body for an already bound key returns 409. Malformed or repeated header fields return 400. JSON whitespace and object order do not change the typed body; optional null and omitted values and omitted versus empty default job lists/maps compare equally. Failed creates do not bind keys. Keys have no expiry and persist in the same controller database across restart. Key lookup precedes duplicate detection. A duplicate match binds a supplied new key to the existing ID.

It returns the original ID instead of queuing work if the original is active (queued, running, or cancelling) or was accepted less than 10 seconds ago. For a deliberate repeat, including automated clients that repeat identical work, send Brewery-Allow-Duplicate: 1 and a new idempotency key. The normal admission checks and same-key replay rules still apply.

It has one boolean for each job kind and the extra capabilities listed below. hf_download is false unless the operator opts in to managed Hugging Face downloads. convert_components is true only if the operator enabled component replacement for a Hugging Face source. custom_profiles is true only if the operator enabled custom profiles with a separate CPU-only converter. gguf_output is true only if the operator set up the GGUF quantizer. gguf_hf_output also requires the bounded Hugging Face exporter. gguf_safetensors_output is a separate opt-in for workers that can pass standalone SafeTensors and a registered assets directory to that exporter. This flag is not a job kind and is not in the aggregate capabilities map. weight_visual enables inventory, tiles, and source-pinned proposals and tuning. weight_hgn enables native HGN sources. weight_packed allows packed weight jobs. weight_safetensors enables standalone SafeTensors and indexed HF weight jobs. An auxiliary then replaces the whole embedded role. It is allowed only on a worker whose capabilities.convert_components is true; otherwise the controller returns 409. A replacement is a registered worker path, not an upload. saved_profile.description: Previously saved controller profile available for review. Not automatically applied to a worker.

managed.description: Compatibility field. Use evaluation.status to distinguish saved profiles from active worker settings.

ready.description: True if the worker allows at least one of benchmark, baseline, evaluate, or generate, through either static configuration or a managed policy. Not a check of any endpoint.

reason.description: Evaluation configuration status, not a host-wide restriction.

approved_ports.description: Loopback ports that the operator approved for this worker.

evaluation_allowed.description: True only if worker policy, GPU load permission and the pinned image allow generate and evaluate. Set by the operator, not by this API.

baseline_allowed.description: False unless worker policy allows managed baseline endpoints.

kind.description: Anthropic Messages or OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions.

base_url.description: HTTPS API base URL, or HTTP on a numeric loopback address. Do not enter credentials, a query, a fragment, or the API operation suffix.

model.description: Provider model ID, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes.

max_tokens.description: Maximum output tokens per request. Cannot exceed max_session_tokens.

max_steps.description: Maximum provider requests and maximum tool calls in one session.

max_session_tokens.description: Total provider-reported input and output token limit. Input use is known only after a request finishes.

host.description: ASCII DNS name or literal IPv4 or IPv6 address, without scheme, brackets or scope.

identity_file.description: Absolute controller-side path to an existing SSH login key. Omit on update to preserve the selection; null clears it. Never send key contents.

fingerprint.description: OpenSSH Ed25519 fingerprint accepted by the operator. Later connections must match this pin.

available.description: A trusted provisioning helper is configured. Not a connectivity test.

AdminToken.description: Worker or runtime ID of the admin catalog.

AdminWorkerAction.description: Move a worker through its lifecycle: unregistered, pending, active, inactive. enroll: unregistered to pending. approve: pending or inactive to active, after a readiness probe. deactivate: active to inactive and hidden from the workbench.

AdminRuntimeAction.description: enable_runtime and install_runtime need the operator's runtime helper and a pinned digest. disable_runtime needs neither. A disabled runtime turns off its capabilities for the worker.

AdminPolicyAction.description: Allow or stop the use of a worker for host auto. It can only lower the pool setting that the operator configured in the dispatch file.

AdminWeightEditorAction.description: Enable or disable the installed local CPU editor or a verified SSH editor. The host policy revision must match. Disabling blocks new jobs; allocated jobs finish on their original executor. This action does not grant access to new source directories.

AdminWeightEditorSetupAction.description: Install and verify a separate editor on an existing admitted SSH worker under its existing pinned trust. On success, the controller saves the verified setup, advances the host policy revision and enables the editor subject to job admission policy. This does not change ordinary RPC, the Hy4 planner, or SSH trust.

revision.description: Echo the current host policy revision from getAdminState.

credential.description: Select an ID from the worker's weight_editor.setup.credentials list. Do not send a key or key path.

EditorModelDirectory.description: Absolute non-root directory on the SSH worker, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes. No empty, dot or dot-dot components, trailing slash, backslash or control characters.

EditorCredentialId.description: Opaque choice returned by getAdminState. A saved SSH login choice includes its definition revision.

label.description: Display label from the SSH definition or the worker-specific credential catalog.

AdminWeightEditorSetup.description: Present for a host with an existing SSH editor transport. Setup verification is separate from enablement and job admission.

model_directory.description: Last saved setup directory, even if verification is no longer valid; null if none is saved.

credentials.description: Eligible verified SSH logins and worker-specific provision credentials. Echo the selected ID; do not send a private key or key path.

blocker.description: Prerequisite for a new installation: the pinned editor runtime or a verified login for this worker. Null if neither is missing.

reason.description: Actionable explanation of the setup blocker, or null.

available.description: A verified editor is available for this control.

enabled.description: Editor configured, independent of admission restrictions.

capabilities.description: Effective host capabilities, not evidence that a particular file or tensor is editable.

pool_ceiling.description: The operator's dispatch setting. allow_pool cannot exceed it.

available.description: True if the operator configured a helper and a pinned digest.

audit.description: Latest entries first. Each holds the action fields and id, at_ms and outcome (started, applied or failed).

unavailable.description: Texts that name what this API does not do: runtime installation without a helper, host provisioning, and resource controls.

ProfileRevision.description: SHA-256 of the canonical recipe. A content address, not a secret.

source_sha256.description: Identity of the checkpoint that the layout was taken from.

base_bytes.description: Catalog size of each built-in profile. A layout estimate.

role.description: For example hyper_connection, routed_expert, rotation_companion or fixed.

delta_bytes.description: Signed bytes, ht43 minus v2, with the companion tensors that change with it. Zero if fixed.

reason.description: Why a tensor is not editable.

name.description: No control characters. Not a built-in name.

overrides.description: Tensor name to the encoding that replaces the base. Each value must differ from base. Each name must be editable. Names are unique.

HgnProfile.description: An HGN profile. Older rows have no format field.

size.description: Layout estimate from the catalog: the base size plus the signed deltas of the overrides. It is not a measured output size.

architecture.description: Saved with the content, so a later catalog cannot change a saved recipe.

GgufPreset.description: An id in presets of getGgufCatalog.

GgufTensorType.description: An id in tensor_types of getGgufCatalog. A raw type that the encoder produces; names that the catalog does not list are refused.

overrides.description: Exact GGUF tensor name (1 to 63 ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen) to a raw tensor type. Floating-point presets (F16, BF16, F32) accept no override. The name is checked against the source inventory when the conversion runs, not when you save.

encoder_revision.description: Revision of the pinned encoder catalog that the profile was checked against.

encoder_family.description: Present when a preset or tensor override requires the separate ROCmFPX encoder. Absent for upstream llama.cpp.

requires_imatrix.description: True if the preset or any override needs an imatrix. The profile has no size estimate: the quantizer decides the exact types per tensor.

NewProfile.description: Choose by format. A body without format is an HGN profile.

encoder.description: Encoder family of the saved revision. Container choice does not change this field.

admission.description: Standard workflow means an existing submission path. It does not establish worker or source eligibility.

stock_preservation.description: By design means that the standard workflow targets the encoder's own container. The preview does not verify an artifact.

experimental_extension.description: Present only for the alternate container. This names an experimental path. It does not establish that an extension is necessary or that a runtime supports it.

encoder_revision.description: Revision of the pinned upstream encoder.

rocmfpx_encoder_revision.description: Revision of the separate ROCmFPX encoder. A preset or override tagged with this family requires a worker with gguf_rocmfpx_output, in addition to the applicable source capabilities. ROCmFPX files require a compatible reader.

presets.description: Named presets, including aliases. Each is a whole-model recipe; the quantizer picks a type for each tensor.

tensor_types.description: Raw tensor types that the encoder can write. Only these can be an override.

source_sha256.description: Lowercase SHA-256 of the registered weight source: the file digest of standalone SafeTensors or the tree digest of an indexed HF snapshot. It is not the digest of the recipe, the output, or the combined source and assets bundle.

layers.description: Maps zero-based layer IDs to tensor types. Keys are canonical decimal unsigned 32-bit integers: no signs or leading zeros. An empty map uses the default for every layer. The exporter checks that the named layers exist and that the requested types fit the source tensors.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of standalone SafeTensors or the indexed HF source tree.

layers.description: At least one layer must select HT3 or HT4. Each trellis-encoded matrix needs both dimensions divisible by 128.

NewConversion.description:
Request for the one-submit workflow inspect, plan, convert and verify. Top-level fields are closed. For HGN output, the input rules and options are the same as for the convert job. The verify stage uses decode_backend. To use a saved custom profile, set profile_revision and do not set options.profile. A custom profile needs a Hugging Face source, the cpu backend for every encoder and for decode_backend, and a worker with capabilities.custom_profiles true; otherwise the controller returns 400 or 409.

Ordinary GGUF output (format gguf, without options.layer_recipe). For hf and gguf sources, input_ids is [source, optional imatrix]. For standalone safetensors, input_ids is [weights, assets, optional imatrix]. The second ID must identify a registered assets directory with model config and tokenizer files. The worker does not search next to the weights file. The weights, assets and any imatrix must be registered on the same worker, and the job must run there. All GGUF workflows need capabilities.gguf_output; hf also needs gguf_hf_output, and safetensors also needs gguf_safetensors_output. The bounded exporter accepts only a small set of dense architectures and rejects Flash-Next. A GGUF source must hold only floating-point weights and be one file. An hgn source is refused. options accepts only preset (an ID from getGgufCatalog; default is the catalog default) and threads. decode_backend and every other option are refused. profile_revision must name a GGUF profile and cannot be combined with options.preset. A preset or tensor type that the catalog marks requires_imatrix needs the imatrix input, or the controller returns 400.

Managed GGUF layer recipe (format gguf, with options.layer_recipe). The recipe is the only option. Submit one indexed HF snapshot ID or [standalone SafeTensors ID, assets directory ID]. Use the source worker, which must also advertise gguf_layer_recipe. Do not use auto, an imatrix, a saved profile or a decode backend.

For either GGUF form, the controller registers artifact_model_id, a gguf model, only after independent verification passes. A GGUF conversion is not a release qualification.

format.description: Output format. HGN with options.layer_recipe uses the managed native HT3/HT4 workflow. HGN without it keeps the ordinary HGN workflow.

host.description: Omitted or null: the source model's host. auto: an eligible worker of the configured quantization pool. Otherwise: that worker.

profile_revision.description: Revision of a saved custom profile. Its format must equal the conversion format. An unknown revision returns 404. The stages use the saved content; the request cannot change it.

then.description: Managed GGUF layer recipe. Supply one indexed HF input, or two inputs in order: standalone SafeTensors weights and a registered assets directory. Both must be on the source worker. There is no imatrix, preset, thread override, saved profile or decode backend. Omit host, use null, or pin the source worker. The worker must advertise gguf_layer_recipe, gguf_output and gguf_hf_output or gguf_safetensors_output as appropriate, and accept all four stages. No eligible worker returns 409. The workflow checks the source digest and uses the same verified layer plan in each stage. It registers the GGUF output only after verification; success is not release qualification.

Managed native HGN HT3/HT4 recipe. Submit an indexed dense Llama or Qwen2 HF source, or standalone SafeTensors followed by registered configuration and tokenizer assets. The same local source worker must advertise hgn_layer_recipe and support all four stages. No imatrix or calibration input is used. The controller registers an hgn-archive only after structural verification. This is not an EXL3 or reference QTIP checkpoint and is not runnable.

ConversionState.description: Workflow state. running includes the time that the active child job waits in the queue. There is no queued state.

duplicate_of.description: Present only when a submission matches an existing conversion by body.

host.description: Concrete worker ID, or auto before assignment of a pool worker.

requested_host.description: Present if auto routing was requested.

format.description: Present only for a GGUF conversion. Absent means HGN.

stage.description: The current stage while running. After a stop, the stage where the workflow stopped or finished.

job_ids.description: IDs of the child jobs, added as each stage is queued. Read each child with getJob.

profile_revision.description: Present if the workflow uses a custom profile.

profile_name.description: Name of that profile at the time of the request.

error.description: Error of the failed child job when the worker gave one. Human-readable, not a stable machine code.

artifact_model_id.description: Model record of the converted output. For GGUF and managed native HGN layer recipes, the controller registers it only after verify passes. Ordinary HGN can register it before verification. Check state.

PlanJob.description: Plan conversion using a registered source and optional auxiliaries. The Hy4 override form reads metadata only and requires one pinned HF source on a dedicated worker that advertises hy4_plan.

ConvertJob.description: Convert a registered source. The only kind that accepts host auto. Auto uses an eligible member of the configured quantization pool, preferring the source host when eligible; without a configured pool, auto uses only the source host. An explicit host is checked against its backend allowlists. Null or omitted host selects the source host, not the auto pool.

Hy4EncodeOptions.description: One pinned, same-worker HF input on a dedicated hy4_encode worker. This form does not allow host auto or a conversion workflow.

VerifyJob.description: Verify converted HGN from a registered source. First input: hf, gguf or hgn source. Second: hgn output. Each further input must be a distinct auxiliary kind (assets, ngram, vision or mtp) selected by its zero-based option index.

VerifyAuxIndex.description: Zero-based index into input_ids; must point to an input of the same kind as this option.

GenerateJob.description: Generate text with a single hgn, brewery-bundle, hgn-v2 or ht43 input. Supply exactly one of an inline prompt or saved prompt ID. The controller accepts up to 65536 UTF-8 bytes, but the bundled evaluator fails jobs whose resolved prompt exceeds 16384 bytes.

max_tokens.description: The bundled evaluator uses 128 when this option is omitted.

EvaluateJob.description: Score one candidate on GSM8K, without a comparison by default. Optionally compare with a saved reference result or the selected worker's configured baseline_source, not both. Ordinary comparisons match the question set and protocol, not the model precision.

BaselineJob.description: Optionally prepare a reference from saved predictions, an evaluation or a baseline result, or from the selected worker's configured baseline_source. A configured source requires an explicit host and no inputs.

baseline_source.description: Worker-configured baseline provider ID from getState, never a URL.

BenchmarkJob.description: Run an operator-configured endpoint target and one or more suites on an explicitly chosen, benchmark-capable host. No model inputs or prompt. Use the target and suite IDs reported by getState for this host; requests cannot provide endpoints or commands.

TransferJob.description: Stage 1 to 32 registered inputs of any kind to an explicit configured destination worker. No options or prompts.

TransferPreviewJob.description: Plan staging for 1 to 32 registered inputs of any kind to an explicit configured destination worker without copying model payloads. No options or prompts.

CacheCleanupJob.description: Remove unpinned staged bundles from the chosen worker's managed cache, limited to one digest if supplied. No input IDs or prompt. Does not delete registered source files.

HfDownloadJob.description: Download from Hugging Face. Omit host or send null to use the built-in backend downloader, which requires no worker enrollment. If the built-in downloader is unavailable, the default request returns 409. An explicit host must have hf_download enabled. No inputs or prompt. The downloader resolves the revision to an immutable commit. A successful verified download registers a new Library model at a persistent backend or worker path.

HfRepoId.description: Hugging Face model repository ID, not a URL.

HfRevision.description: Branch, tag, or commit. A full lowercase hexadecimal commit must match the resolved commit.

HfFilename.description: Exact relative file name within the repository; no glob or local path.

filename.description: Omit to download the full checkpoint.

PackedWeightOptIn.description: Opt in to fixed-scale packed operations for GGUF Q4_0 or Q8_0, or HGN Q8G64. Requires weight_packed and all other applicable worker capabilities. Omit for the legacy floating-point mode. A successful packed job returns packed: true. A packed proposal or tune report gives the dtype and realized before and after values for each edit.

WeightSingleSource.description: The input is a Library ID for GGUF, single-file HGN (kind hgn), standalone SafeTensors (kind safetensors), or an indexed HF checkpoint directory (kind hf) on the selected worker. HGN requires weight_hgn. SafeTensors and HF require weight_safetensors and do not support packed mode. These capabilities are additional to the per-job opt-in.

Exl3LayerJob.description: Encode one exact dense F16/BF16/F32 128x128 [out,in] tensor from a standalone SafeTensors file on the source worker. This is uncalibrated layer encoding, not model conversion. The worker requires BREWERY_WEIGHT_SAFETENSORS=1, an explicit BREWERY_WEIGHT_SAFETENSORS_VERIFY_BYTES limit of at most 64 MiB, and a canonical native CLI configured in BREWERY_EXL3_CHECKPOINT. Encoding uses CPU; the requested backend performs forward verification without fallback. The result is one layer artifact, not a Library model.

source_sha256.description: File SHA-256 from the weight inventory.

WeightInspectJob.description: Read one scalar, a tensor inventory page, or a tensor tile from a registered weight source. Inventory and tiles also require weight_visual on the selected worker. Tiles use the inventory's source digest; later inventory pages can use that digest too. For standalone SafeTensors, the digest is the file SHA-256. For indexed HF, it is the canonical bundle SHA-256. A source mismatch fails the job without publishing values.

shape.description: Same rank as origin. Rank 1: up to 1024 elements. Rank 2–4: the last two dimensions are at most 32 each; all leading dimensions equal 1.

WeightProposeJob.description: Prepare a proposal for a registered weight source without writing model weights. HGN, SafeTensors, and HF receipts identify source_format as the Library kind.

source_sha256.description: Use the inspected source digest for edits based on a visual read. Requires weight_visual.

WeightTuneJob.description: Prepare a proposal for selected coordinates in a rank-two tensor. Inputs are a registered weight source (GGUF, single-file HGN, standalone SafeTensors, or indexed HF), calibration, and held-out data in that order. Use two distinct weight-calibration records. All inputs must be on the same opted-in worker. HGN requires weight_hgn. SafeTensors and HF require weight_safetensors and do not support packed mode.

source_sha256.description: Use the inspected source digest for tuning based on a visual read. Requires weight_visual.

WeightApplyJob.description: Confirm review of an existing successful proposal or tune job. Its source and worker must match the input record exactly. The controller supplies the proposal to the worker and derives packed intent from the reviewed job. A packed apply needs weight_packed and must confirm the exact approved proposal digest. A verified result registers a new model of the same kind without overwriting the original. A failed or cancelled apply does not register an artifact.

WeightApplyResult.description: The worker verified an edit in the registered source format. The artifact must have the same kind as the source and be in this job's work directory. SafeTensors and HF require the exact approved proposal digest. HF output retains every source manifest member and its size; ancillary files are unchanged. The bundle digest is SHA-256 over sorted relative path, NUL, decimal bytes, NUL, lowercase file SHA-256, newline records. Registration is not a quality or release verdict.

path.description: Canonical relative file path in the checkpoint.

HfDownloadResult.description: Verified download registered in the Library. The artifact path is under this job's managed download directory on the worker.

tensor.description: Use an exact SafeTensors or GGUF tensor name.
Use an exact SafeTensors or GGUF tensor name.

delta.description: Source minus reference when both tensor shapes match and both measurements exist.

JobResult.description: Worker result. Weight apply and Hugging Face download check output identity and register a Library model only on verified success. A job result is not a release verdict.

configurations.description: Configurations in score order. The signed cosine is from the original directions before orthogonalization.

position.description: Optional source token position. This is provenance only; it does not change the weight edit.

provenance.description: Free text, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes. It is visible to agents; do not include secrets.

selected_layer.description: Layer with the highest positive held-out Cohen's d in version 2, or the highest positive raw margin in version 1. Null if none qualifies.

held_out_cohens_d.description: Raw margin divided by the pooled within-class sample standard deviation of held-out projections. Null if undefined.

mean_residual_norm.description: Mean L2 norm of l_out over both held-out classes and all captured positions, after stream sum but before normalization on HGN.

negative_mean.description: Mean negative-class activation over training prompts. Required for projected ablation; older artifacts omit it.

path.description: Path on the worker, not an API download URL.

report.description: Native converter report. Inspect describes the source; plan adds plan and layouts; convert reports publication; verify reports source/output checks.

status.description: Aggregate suite coverage, separate from the controller job state.
